chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Who played on the Morton and Crawley session, and Morton's bands
summary: The studio was full of familiar musicians, Holmes can't separate Russell's men from Morton's, and it was his only recording with Morton.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: And you were there because you were with Russell at the Victor recording.
Yeah. I was part of Russell's band. That's what I was.
So do you remember who Jelly brought in with him, any of the musicians?
I don't know, because we were all there together. See, all us musicians knew one another. Now, see, just like I know you and...
Yeah.

Well, I come with my band and here you come in with somebody else's band, but we all know one another. So it's hard to distinguish who come with who, or what, you know. But we're all playing together. Some numbers I played, some numbers the other guys played. I know there was a bunch of us around in the studio that morning. There was a bunch of us. There had to be. There was a string bass and a tuba on one of the recordings. We were so many that sometimes, you know, they would be recording, and Russell would tell me, "All right, Charlie, you're in this number," you know, and I'd go up there and play...
You remember that Barbarin was there, I suppose.
Yeah, sure.
Do you remember any other drummer?
Oh, I don't know.
Well, it's hard to...

Usually I wasn't thinking about what instruments they were playing, unless I actually heard them or saw them or one of them things. It's just like you'd meet a bunch...like you go around to a club meeting, and you meet a bunch of the guys that you don't know what they're playin', but you talk to 'em anyway. You know, they know you, you know them -- you talk. You don't stop to think of what instrument he's playin'. Music was the last thing we
thought about. That's the only reason we were there, was the music. We were there to socialize (?) a little bit(?).
As far as Morton was concerned, this was the only date you actually recorded with him.
That's about the only time I recorded with him, yeah.
Did you gig with him at all?
No.
Because he was always getting bands together.
I know. He had bands. In fact, I think he used Chick Webb's band sometimes. And other little bands he'd play around with. I don't know, did Clyde work with him?
With Morton? No.
No. He never said anything about him. He didn't work with him... He didn't say nothin' about it.
He used Bill Benford's band, so Tommy Benford was with him.
Tommy Benford's brother?
Yeah.
Yeah, I know Jelly Roll. He used quite a few bands, you know. At that time, anybody who had a job had a band.
